headline: Held-out validation of machine learning endpoint prediction across biological conditions
label: Predictive Models For Biomedical Endpoints
summary: Recent work evaluates endpoint models under realistic held-out conditions, from unseen hospitals to multiple permeability assays.
synthesis: The dominant thread is supervised prediction of biological and pharmacological endpoints, assessed through external or structured validation. Masked autoencoder and chemical language-model encodings improve MALDI-TOF resistance prediction on unseen hospitals and periods. LLM-guided literature gene prioritization for sepsis is validated on VANISH mortality data and extended to semaglutide serum proteomics. PCPpred predicts modified peptide permeability across PAMPA, Caco-2, MDCK and RRCK assays. BIPE regresses peptide bitterness intensity in log space against electronic tongue and sensory data, and the sodium-iodide symporter study combines docking-based screening with RF, XGB and SVM models on ECFP4 and CDDD features. The quantum projective learning preprint is distinctive in pairing antibiotic resistance prediction in urine cultures with a data complexity signature that flags when quantum learning outperforms classical models. Modality and endpoint vary across items, so the shared element is evaluation under realistic conditions rather than a common architecture.
